title: The lifecycle API
description: What any service implementing the Agent Development Lifecycle answers, so that one client works against more than one service. Every request and answer is JSON, at the path /v1/lifecycle on the service. Times are ISO 8601 with a zone. Auth is Authorization: Bearer <key>, where the key is one the person makes for their own account, as the service says. A build lists every stage of stages.json, one entry each, and a stage the service does not run is reported as not_offered. A client draws one button for each action the build offers, and nothing else. An organization chooses who holds each role of stages.json (the roles operations): the service's reference agent, its own agent, a contracted supplier, a person or an outside tool. A holder outside the service hands its evidence back in one of the open formats stages.json lists, and the service reads it onto the stage. An organization also chooses which stages its lifecycle uses (the stages operations), for the whole organization or for one project; when nothing is chosen every stage is used, and a build keeps the choice in effect when it started. The schema changes only by adding: a client ignores a field it does not know, and a service never removes or retypes one. Version 0.2 adds the roles operations, the evidence operation and new fields, and it also adds values to two lists, the holder's kinds and the stage's states; a client that does not know a state draws the stage as not_offered, and one that does not know a holder's kind shows the holder's name. Version 0.3 adds the stages operations, the state not_used, and the build's lifecycle field; a client that knows only 0.2 draws a not_used stage as not_offered. Version 0.4 adds products, stage workspaces, each stage's chat and the build's artifacts: a product is every build of one name, one build per version; each stage of a build is a workspace with what it was given, what it handed back as versioned artifacts, and its gate; and each stage has a chat with the agent holding it, kept per product per stage across builds. Answering in a chat changes nothing: a change the person asks for comes back as a proposal of the build's existing action, which the person takes with the actions operation, so a change always goes back through its gate. A client that knows only 0.3 ignores the artifacts field, and a service that does not offer the 0.4 operations answers them 404. Version 0.4.1 adds the product's boss (Agent Roles, role-boss): a conversation at the product level with an agent that answers from the product's record, routes a directive into the chat of the stage that owns it, and plans a larger request across the stages, proposing each stage's existing action; it never answers a gate, never changes an artifact, and lists everything it committed on the person's behalf. A service that does not offer the boss answers its operations 404. Version 0.4.2 adds each stage's cadence from stages.json 1.3.0 (every_build, setup or when_needed) to the build's stages and the stage workspace; carried, on a setup stage whose holder and settings are the same as an earlier version's; and two lists on a product: setup, each stage set up once per product with its holder, settings and the version it has held since, and when_needed, each action on the product with whether the service can run it now and, when it cannot, why. A client shows a build's steps from its every_build stages, and the others on the product. A client that knows only 0.4.1 ignores them. Version 0.4.3 adds features: the statement of the job carries a feature list, each feature with a stable id, a name, what it does and the offering it belongs to. A stage's agent or the boss proposes a new or changed feature in a reply (features), and the person approves it there, one feature at a time, as a recorded gate decision of Requirements, or says not now, which keeps it proposed as a backlog item; a person who may not answer Requirements asks an approver instead. Tests name the feature they check, a round of the gate reports its results per feature, and a matrix shows each feature against the spec, the tests, the code, the review and the docs, with each feature's history across the stages. A service that does not offer features answers their operations 404. Version 0.4.4 adds the guided setup and the when-needed actions: each setup item carries a form (who may hold it, a few settings with defaults, and the question a client sends the boss), saved with the roles operations, each stage's settings under its own id in the holder's settings; each when-needed item a service can run carries its needs and a confirm card (what will happen in the stage's words, who may act, the versions it acts on and what cannot be undone), is taken with the actions operation on the build it names, and answers a result that the product keeps as the item's last; and the product says which version runs and whether it is retired. How a service hands rollback, reconfigure and retire to the runtime it is given is runtime-verbs.md. A client that knows only 0.4.3 ignores them. Version 0.4.5 makes features visible at every stage: each every-build stage of a build, and its workspace, carry the stage's features (Requirements: approved of all; Test: tests per feature, a feature with none to do; Code: passing per feature; Review: findings tied to a feature through its tests, the rest not tied; Docs: which features the docs name); a matrix row carries its pending proposal, where it was proposed and the tests that check it, and the matrix the tests that check no feature; and a product made before features can have them listed from its statement of the job by the spec writer (backfill), with the tests already in the build mapped to them where their names or content make it clear and the rest left unmapped, then approved one at a time or together (approve_all). A client that knows only 0.4.4 ignores them. Version 0.4.6 adds starting from existing code (stages.json 1.4.0, Reverse engineering): a start request may name the starting point existing-code and the codebase (a repository and commit, or a local folder for local use); the build enters at Reverse engineering, whose as-built record is one artifact of kind as_built with a readable summary per part; each behavior in it reaches Requirements as a proposed feature marked as built, which the person approves as intended, marks as a bug (kept as a proposed fix item linked to the behavior, never approved silently) or drops; and the build and the product say which commit of the codebase each build knew, so a client can see when the code changed outside the lifecycle. A client that knows only 0.4.5 ignores them. Version 0.4.7 adds starting from an as-built record (stages.json 1.5.0): a start request may name the starting point as-built-record and the record (a local folder of its files, or a repository, a commit and the path of the record in it), to build again code kept elsewhere without taking that code on, as in a rewrite, a port or a clean-room rebuild; the build enters at Requirements, the record is its as_built artifact, saying where it was brought from, and each behavior in it reaches Requirements as a proposed feature marked as built, answered as with existing code; there is no adoption, so Code writes the code fresh. It also adds the action back_to_requirements, offered at Code wherever back_to_test is offered and also when Code was refused, with the person's words: Requirements opens again with the words as an ask for changes, and once the person approves the revised spec, Test revises the suite against it and Code goes on, all recorded as a deviation. A client that knows only 0.4.6 ignores them, and draws back_to_requirements as it draws any action. Version 0.4.8 adds the spec (stages.json 1.6.0, standards/spec.schema.json): what Requirements hands back is the spec, the analysis of the product's functional requirements and capabilities, an artifact of kind spec with a readable summary (SpecSummary): each feature with its requirements and acceptance scenarios, the interfaces, the constraints and the open questions. The agent's own files a package is built from (the statement artifact, StatementSummary) are made at Design from the spec. A client that knows only 0.4.7 reads a spec artifact's summary.words. Version 0.4.9 adds the holder's skills: a stage workspace's holder may list each of its skills by name, with its one-line description and its SKILL.md in full, or say in one sentence why the service cannot see them. A client that knows only 0.4.8 ignores them. Version 0.4.10 adds feature runs: once a version's spec is approved, each approved feature may be made in a run of its own (its suite, its code and the person's OK), at the same time as the others, each with its own pull request; the build answers each as a FeatureRun (feature_runs), the build list one card per run, an action names the run it acts on (run), and a timeline bar the run it is of. The build's own stages, actions and timeline read across the runs. A client that knows only 0.4.9 ignores them. The operations list names the definition each request and answer must match; lifecycle-api-check.mjs checks a running service against it, together with the rules a schema cannot say.

operations.does: Who is asking, and the service's name.
The person's builds, each with the stage it is at and where it ended, in words. A build the person archived is left out unless the request adds ?archived=1.
Start a build from the person's words.
One build, stage by stage, with its log and the actions it offers now.
The build's run as one bar per step per round, ordered by start, with how long each took and the totals by kind. Added in 0.1.
A file a stage handed back, at the link the build gives.

Take one of the actions the build offers, with the inputs it needs. From 0.4.4 it also takes a product's when-needed action (name is the when_needed stage's id: impact, retract, reconfigure, rollback or decommission) on the build the product's when_needed list names, with the needs that item's action lists, once the person has read its confirm card; the answer then adds result. It answers 403 in words to a person the lifecycle does not let take it, 400 for a need left empty, and 409 when it is not offered on that build now, or when the holder it runs through (such as the runtime) refuses, with the holder's words; a refusal is kept on the build like a result.
Send one input to the build's pull request or to the installed agent, and read the answer.
The tries made on a build, newest first.
Keep a try: it is added to the agent's suite as a new test file.
Say a try came back wrong: it goes back to whoever holds Code, as a comment on the pull request.

Hand back evidence for a stage held outside the service, in one of the formats stages.json lists. The service reads it and lists it on that stage. It answers 400 when the content does not read as the format named. Added in 0.2.
Every role of stages.json, each with who holds it now and where that binding comes from. With ?project=<name>, as a build started under that project would see them. Added in 0.2.

Bind a role for the organization, or with ?project=<name> for builds started under that project. It answers 400 for a role stages.json does not name, a your_agent or contracted holder with no handle, the requester bound to anyone but a person, or an evidence format stages.json does not list. Added in 0.2.

Remove the organization's binding of a role, or with ?project=<name> that project's, so the role falls back to the organization's binding, then to the service's reference agent, then to nobody. Added in 0.2.

Every stage of stages.json, in its order, each saying whether the organization's lifecycle uses it, where that choice comes from, and whether this service can run its builds without it. With ?project=<name>, as a build started under that project would see them. When nothing is chosen, every stage is used. Added in 0.3.

Choose whether the organization's lifecycle uses a stage, or with ?project=<name> whether that project's does. A build started later keeps the choice; a build already started does not change. It answers 400 for a stage stages.json does not name, or for used: false on a stage this service cannot leave out; 403 for a member who is not an admin of the organization; and 409 when the choice could not be saved. Added in 0.3.

Remove the organization's choice for a stage, or with ?project=<name> that project's, so the stage falls back to the organization's choice, then to the default, which uses it. It answers 403 and 409 as PUT does. Added in 0.3.
Every product: the builds of one name, each product with its newest build and its versions. A product whose builds are all archived is left out unless the request adds ?archived=1. Added in 0.4.

One product: its builds, newest first, the run plan of its newest build that has one, and a short activity feed, one line per stage event, newest first. From 0.4.2 it also lists the product's setup stages, each with its holder, settings and the version it has held since, and its when_needed stages, each with whether the service can run it now. It answers 404 for a name no build has. Added in 0.4.

One stage of a build as a workspace: what it was given (earlier stages' artifacts), what it handed back (its artifacts), what done means for it, and its gate. It answers 404 for a stage stages.json does not name. Added in 0.4.

The chat with the agent holding a stage, across the product's builds, oldest first, each message naming the build and version it was said in. A gate is not a message: it is on the stage's workspace. Added in 0.4.

Say something to the agent holding a stage, on the product's newest build or the build named. The agent answers in words from the stage's outputs, what it was given and the build's record, and the person's message and the reply are kept. Answering changes nothing. When the person asks for a change, the reply proposes the build's existing action for it with its needs filled, only when the person may take that action now. Anyone who may read the build may post. It answers 400 in words for a stage the build's lifecycle leaves out or one held by a person, an outside tool or anyone the service cannot send messages to, and 409 when no agent can answer now, such as when the model is not set. Added in 0.4.

The conversation with the product's boss (Agent Roles, role-boss), oldest first, each message naming the product's newest build and its version when it was said. A proposal kept on a message says whether it is still open. Added in 0.4.1.

Say something to the product's boss, or confirm or decline one of its proposals. It answers from the product's record; routes a directive into the chat of the stage that owns it and says where it went (routed); breaks a larger request into a plan naming each stage in order and the gate the person meets at each (plan); and proposes the first stage's existing action, or first the start of the next version when the request changes the agent's statement (proposes). It never answers a gate, never changes an artifact, and takes no action: a stage's action is taken with the actions operation, and the next version starts only when the person confirms that proposal here (started). Anyone who may read the product may post; a proposal of a gate's action is made only to a person who may answer that gate. It answers 400 in words for an empty message or a proposal that is not open, and 409 when the boss cannot answer now, such as when the model is not set. Added in 0.4.1.

Everything the boss committed on the person's behalf, oldest first, in full: each message it posted into a stage's chat, each proposal with the person's answer, each build it started with the confirmation it started it on, and each stage it told to drop work. Added in 0.4.1.

The build's features as a matrix: one row per feature the build carries, one cell per column (spec, tests, code, review, docs) saying whether that artifact covers it, and a badge saying whether the feature is new, changed or unchanged in this build's version. Added in 0.4.3.

Approve one proposed feature: a gate decision of Requirements for that feature alone, recorded with who gave it, when, and the message it was given on. The statement of the job gets a new version with the feature in it. Only a person who may answer the Requirements gate may approve; anyone else gets 403 in words, and asks instead. It answers 400 in words for a proposal that is not open. Added in 0.4.3.
Leave one proposed feature for later: it stays proposed, as a backlog item linked to the conversation it came from. Anyone who may read the build may say not now. Added in 0.4.3.
Ask the people who may answer the Requirements gate to approve one proposed feature. Each is told through the service's notices, and sees the same proposal with its approve button. Added in 0.4.3.
The product's features as a matrix, for its newest build, or with ?version=<version> for the build of that version. Added in 0.4.3.

One feature of the product and its history across the stages and the versions, oldest first: proposed in a chat, approved, tests added, code changed, reviewed, docs updated, each entry linked to the message or the artifact. It answers 404 for a feature the product does not have. Added in 0.4.3.

List the features of a product made before features existed. The person's message goes to the agent holding Requirements, the spec writer, in that stage's chat; its reply proposes every feature of the statement of the job (features), each with id, name, what it does and its offering, and the tests already in the build that clearly check it (tests). They arrive as proposed, to approve one at a time or together. It answers 409 in words when it is not offered (the features matrix's backfill says why). Added in 0.4.5.

Approve several proposed features at once, such as those listed after the build: each a recorded gate decision of Requirements as one approved in a chat, together one new version of the statement of the job. Only a person who may answer the Requirements gate may; anyone else gets 403 in words. It answers 400 in words, approving none, when any proposal is not open. Added in 0.4.5.

Say that one behavior proposed as built is a bug: what the code does is not what is wanted. The proposal is answered bug, and a proposed fix item linked to the behavior is kept, with the person's words; the behavior is not approved, so it is not pinned by a test, and the fix item is never approved by this answer or by the Requirements gate. Only a person who may answer the Requirements gate may; anyone else gets 403 in words. It answers 400 in words for a proposal that is not open or not marked as built. Added in 0.4.6.

Drop one behavior proposed as built: it is not kept, so the statement does not carry it and no test pins it. Only a person who may answer the Requirements gate may; anyone else gets 403 in words. It answers 400 in words for a proposal that is not open or not marked as built. Added in 0.4.6.

Time.description: ISO 8601, with a zone (Z or an offset).

StageId.description: An id from stages.json, such as "code".

State.description: waiting_on_you: the person's act is next. not_offered: this service cannot hand the stage to anyone, even if its role were bound. not_bound: the stage applies to the build, nobody holds its role, and the service does not run it (added in 0.2). not_applicable: the stage does not apply to this kind of build, such as Review on a process (added in 0.2). not_used: the build's lifecycle leaves the stage out; the stage has no holder, has run 0 times, offers no action, and its given says "Not part of this build's lifecycle" with whose choice it was, the organization's default or the project's name (added in 0.3). When more than one could apply, not_applicable comes first, then not_used, then every other state. A stage held outside the service is not_started until its evidence or answer arrives, then done, or refused when the evidence says it failed. A client that does not know a state draws it as not_offered.

RoleId.description: A role id from stages.json, such as "code-critic". Added in 0.2.

Cadence.description: A stage's cadence, its cadence in stages.json (added in 1.3.0). every_build: the stage runs on every build of the product, the routine. setup: the stage is set up once per product, and its holder and settings are carried forward to each later version until someone changes them. when_needed: an action on the product, run when something happens, not as part of a build. Added in 0.4.2.

Carried.description: A setup stage whose holder and settings are the same as an earlier version's, so nothing is asked again: the version it has held since, and the words a person reads, such as "Unchanged since 0.1.0". Absent on a stage set up anew in this build, and on any stage that is not setup. Added in 0.4.2.

since.description: The version of the product's earliest build, in an unbroken run of builds up to this one, whose holder and settings for the stage are the same as this build's.

EvidenceFormat.description: An evidence format from stages.json's evidence_formats. Added in 0.2.

ErrorAnswer.description: Any 4xx or 5xx answer. A 401 or 403 means the key is missing, wrong or lacks what the call needs.

error.description: What went wrong, in words a person can read.

build.description: On a refused action, the build as it now stands.

tries_today.description: On a 429 from try: the tries this build has had today.

tries_cap.description: On a 429 from try: the most tries a build may have in a day.

name.description: The service's name as a person should see it.

kind.description: What the build makes: an agent, shaped as a Common Agent, or a process, shaped as an Agent Processes document. Absent means agent. Added in 0.1.

at.description: The stage the build is at, and its state there.

summary.description: Where the build ended, or where it is, in the words a person reads first, such as "Installed · conforms", "Installed · paused: failed conformance", "Waiting on you at Code" or "Stopped at Requirements". Added in 0.1; a client that finds none says the stage and state.

archived.description: The person archived it. Archived builds are listed only when the request adds ?archived=1. Added in 0.1.

feature_runs.description: For a version whose features are made in runs of their own, one card per run, in the order the runs started, so a board can show each as a card of its own beside the build. Absent for a build made in one run. Added in 0.4.10.

FeatureRunCard.description: One feature of a version made in a run of its own, as a board shows it: which feature, and where its run is. Added in 0.4.10.

id.description: The run's id on the build, such as F3, or F3-2 for the second run of the same feature. An action names it as run.

feature.description: The feature the run makes, by its id; all for the one run that makes a spec with no features.

name.description: The feature in words, its id and its name, such as "F3 Count lines".

started.description: When the run started: at the spec's approval, or at the feature's own approval after it.

ended.description: True once the run has closed: the person's OK merged it, or it was stopped.

FeatureRunAt.description: The stage a feature run is at, and its state there, as BuildListItem.at says it for a build. Added in 0.4.10.

summary.description: Where the run is, in words, such as "Waiting on you at Code".

FeatureRun.description: One feature of a version made in a run of its own, on the build answer: its card (FeatureRunCard), with its own stages (Test and Code), the actions it offers, its pull request, its log and its timeline. Added in 0.4.10.

by.description: Who the run is held for: the build's owner.

stages.description: The stages the run holds, in the order of stages.json, each once.

actions.description: What the person may do on this run now, each naming it as run; the same actions are on the build's own list. Empty once the run has ended.

pull_request.description: The run's own pull request, when Code is on one.

timeline.description: The run's own bars, ordered by start.

kind.description: What to build. Absent means agent. A service that does not build the kind asked for refuses the request and says so. Added in 0.1.

does.description: What the agent does, or what the process gets done, in the person's words.

more.description: Anything else the person wants said.

name.description: A name for the agent, when the person has one.

prototype.description: A public repository, as owner/name, to read as the agent's prototype.

project.description: The project the build is for, in the person's words. A role bound for that project holds its stages in place of the organization's binding. Added in 0.2.

starting_point.description: What the person brings, as the id of one of stages.json's starting_points, such as idea, existing-code or as-built-record; absent means idea. With existing-code the build enters at Reverse engineering and source names the codebase; does may then be words the client writes, such as "Adopt the existing code of word-counter". With as-built-record (added in 0.4.7) the build enters at Requirements and source names the as-built record of code kept elsewhere, which is built again without being taken on; does may be words the client writes, such as "Rebuild word-counter from its as-built record". A service that does not start from the point named refuses the request and says so. Added in 0.4.6.

source.description: The codebase, for the starting point existing-code; the as-built record, for the starting point as-built-record (added in 0.4.7). Added in 0.4.6.

result.description: What a when-needed action did, when the request took one. Added in 0.4.4.

ActionResult.description: What a when-needed action did, in words, and what it handed back. The same is kept on the build as the stage's record, so it shows in the product's activity and as the item's last. Added in 0.4.4.

cannot_undo.description: For Rollback: the side effects that are not undone, the card's and any the holder named.

files.description: What it handed back, read with GET /builds/{id}/files?path=<path>, such as impact/impact-report.md.

report.description: For Impact: the impact report the impact analyst handed back, as Markdown.

kind.description: What the build makes: an agent, shaped as a Common Agent, or a process, shaped as an Agent Processes document. Absent means agent. Added in 0.1.

handle.description: The address the agent answers at once it is installed. For a process, the address of the installed process document.

stages.description: One entry for each of the stages in stages.json.

actions.description: Everything the person may do now. A client draws one button for each, and nothing else.

can_try.description: Whether a try may be sent now, against the pull request and against the installed agent.

summary.description: Where the build ended, or where it is, in words: the same words as the list's at.summary. Added in 0.1.

paused.description: The installed agent is paused, since when and why (for example, a conformance check it failed); null when it is not. Added in 0.1.

archived.description: The person archived it. Added in 0.1.

project.description: The project the build was started under, as its StartRequest gave it; absent when none was given. Added in 0.2.

lifecycle.description: Whose choice of stages the build started under, and when it took it. The build keeps that choice: a stage chosen or left out later does not change it. Absent from a service that keeps no choice of stages. Added in 0.3.

project.description: The project whose stages the build took, the same as the build's project; null when the build named none, so it took the organization's choices and the default.

at.description: When the build took the choice: when it started.

timeline.description: The build's run as one bar per step per round, ordered by start; empty when the service keeps no run for it. Steps that run at the same time keep their own bars, so overlaps show. Added in 0.1.

artifacts.description: What the build has made and will make, in stage order, only for stages its lifecycle uses. Added in 0.4.

source.description: The codebase this build knew, at the commit it knew: for a build started from existing code, the commit it was adopted or reverse engineered at; for a build started from an as-built record (added in 0.4.7), the code the record describes, at the commit the record names, with where the record was read. Absent for a build that knew no codebase. Added in 0.4.6.

feature_runs.description: For a version whose features are made in runs of their own, each run, in the order they started: once the spec is approved, each approved feature runs its own Test and Code at the same time as the others, with its own pull request and the person's OK, and a feature approved later starts its run then. The version waits for every run to close before Package. The build's own Test and Code read across the runs, its actions include each open run's, and its timeline each run's bars, so a client that knows only 0.4.9 still shows the build. Absent for a build made in one run. Added in 0.4.10.

phase.description: The step of the run, by the process document's name for it.

round.description: 1 the first time the step ran, one more each time it ran again.

holder.description: Who held it, by handle; null for a person's gate.

kind.description: agent: an agent working. person: waiting on a person. external: waiting on something outside the run (a pull request, a sandbox, an install, a verdict).

end.description: Null while it is still open.

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds from start to end; null while it is still open.

status.description: How it stands or ended, such as closed, working or superseded.

run.description: On a build's timeline, the feature run the bar is of (feature_runs[].id); absent for the build's own run. Added in 0.4.10.

total_ms.description: From the first bar's start to the last bar's end.

by_kind_ms.description: The bars' own time summed by kind: agent, person, external.

share.description: Each kind's part of the bars' summed time, 0 to 1.

totals.description: Null when the service keeps no run for the build.

holder.description: Who holds the stage; null for a stage that is not offered, not bound, not applicable or not used.

runs.description: How many times the stage has run.

done_when_met.description: Whether the stage's "done when" was met; null when it is not known yet.

where.description: Where the stage's work is, when it is somewhere the person can open.

evidence.description: The evidence handed back for the stage by a holder outside the service, as the service read it. Added in 0.2.

cadence.description: The stage's cadence in stages.json. Added in 0.4.2.

carried.description: On a setup stage whose holder and settings are unchanged from an earlier version. Added in 0.4.2.

features.description: How many of the product's features the stage covers on this build, for a short count beside the stage, such as "4 of 5 features". Present on an every-build stage that has made its artifact, when the build carries features. Added in 0.4.5.

Evidence.description: One piece of evidence, as the service read it. Added in 0.2.

name.description: Its name, as it was handed back.

summary.description: What the service read in it, in words, such as "2 errors, 5 warnings" or "41 components".

file.description: The file as it was handed back.

kind.description: reference_agent: the service's own agent for the role. your_agent: an agent of the organization's, on the mesh. contracted: a supplier's agent the organization contracted, on the mesh. person: a person. outside_tool: a tool outside the mesh, whose evidence is handed back to the service. contracted and outside_tool were added in 0.2.

name.description: Words a person reads, such as "CodeRabbit" or "Our security team".

handle.description: The holder's handle on the mesh. A your_agent or contracted holder has one, a reference_agent may, and a person or an outside_tool has none. Added in 0.2.

role.description: The role it holds the stage as. Added in 0.2.

evidence.description: The evidence the holder hands back, and where it can be read. Added in 0.2.

where.description: Words or an address saying where the holder's evidence can be read.

skills.description: The holder's skills, each once, as the service can read them, such as a reference agent's skills folder. Given on a stage workspace's holder; a service may leave it out where a holder is listed many times, such as on a build's stages. An empty list says the holder has no skills of its own; absent says nothing about them. Added in 0.4.9.

skills_note.description: In place of skills, when the service cannot see them, why in one sentence, such as "Its skills are whatever your coding harness has installed." Added in 0.4.9.

Skill.description: One skill of a holder, as its SKILL.md says it (the Agent Skills format: frontmatter with a name and a description, then the instructions). Added in 0.4.9.

name.description: The skill's name, from its frontmatter, or its folder's name when the frontmatter has none.

description.description: Its one-line description, from its frontmatter, when it has one.

text.description: The SKILL.md as written, in full, frontmatter and all. It comes with the answer, because a skill is not a file of the build that the files operation reads.

RolesAnswer.description: Every role of stages.json, once each. Added in 0.2.

project.description: The project asked about, when the request named one.

Role.description: One role, as stages.json names it, and who holds it now. Added in 0.2.

offering.description: The offering a bound handle is sent the stage's input under, role-<id>.

binding.description: The binding in effect; null when nobody holds the role.

from.description: Where the binding in effect comes from: the project's binding, the organization's, the service's default (its reference agent, or the person who asked for the requester), or nobody.

reference_agent.description: The service's own agent for the role, when it runs one.

RoleBinding.description: Who holds a role. scope, since and by are absent on a default, which nobody bound. Added in 0.2.

scope.description: { "org": true } for the organization's binding, or { "project": <name> } for one project's.

RoleBindingRequest.description: The holder to bind the role to. Added in 0.2.

StagesAnswer.description: Every stage of stages.json, once each, in its order, and whether the lifecycle uses it. Added in 0.3.

project.description: The project asked about; null when the request named none.

updated_at.description: When a choice this answer reads was last changed; absent when nobody has chosen.

StageChoice.description: One stage, as stages.json names it, and whether the lifecycle uses it. Added in 0.3.

phase.description: The id of the stage's phase in stages.json, such as "define".

roles.description: The roles that hold the stage, its role_ids in stages.json. Who holds each is in the roles answer.

used.description: Whether the lifecycle uses the stage. A build started now runs a used stage and reports an unused one as not_used.

from.description: Where the choice comes from: the project's, the organization's, or the default, which uses every stage.

can_leave_out.description: Whether this service can run its builds without the stage: false when a kind of build it makes, to which the stage applies, needs it. A fact about the service, not a rule of the organization's.

why_not.description: When can_leave_out is false, what needs the stage, in words a person reads, such as "Code is written to Test's suite; this service cannot build without it."

StageChoiceRequest.description: Whether the lifecycle uses the stage. Added in 0.3.

EvidenceRequest.description: Evidence for one stage of a build. Added in 0.2.

name.description: Its name, such as the file's name.

content.description: The file, as a JSON value or as a base64 string.

back.description: True when this round sent the work back.

by_feature.description: A round that ran the suite: its results for each feature the suite's tests name, a test naming its feature by starting with the feature's id in square brackets, such as "[F3] counts an empty passage as none". Added in 0.4.3.

link.description: Where its bytes are read, with the same key: an address, or a path on the service such as /v1/lifecycle/builds/{id}/files?path={path}.

head.description: The pull request's newest commit, as a short sha.

Check.description: The check on the pull request's newest commit.

stage.description: The stage it acts at, one the build offers.

name.description: Posted as /builds/{id}/actions/{name}. Names a service may offer include approve, changes, accept, resume, back_to_test, back_to_requirements and stop; archive and unarchive, for a build that ended without an install; and resume_agent, which resumes an installed agent a failed conformance check paused. back_to_requirements (added in 0.4.7) acts at Code, wherever back_to_test is offered and also when Code was refused, and needs the person's words (kind words): Requirements opens again with them as an ask for changes; once the person approves the revised spec, Test revises the suite against it, and Code goes on (on a pull request, on the same branch, with the revised spec and suite as one forward commit). The service records it as a deviation, as it records back_to_test.

run.description: The feature run it acts on (feature_runs[].id), for a version whose features are made in runs of their own. A client sends it back as run in the action's request; a service given none takes the version's own action of that name, else the first run that offers it. Absent: the build's own. Added in 0.4.10.

name.description: The member it is sent as in the action's request.

kind.description: text (a line), words (a paragraph) or repository (owner/name); from 0.4.4 also choice, one of options.

optional.description: True when the person may leave it empty, and it is then not sent.

options.description: For a choice: what the person may choose from. Added in 0.4.4.

default.description: What is filled in before the person changes it. Added in 0.4.4.

ActionRequest.description: One member for each need the action names, as words. A need marked optional and left empty is not sent. From 0.4.10 it may also carry run: the feature run the action is for, as the action named it.

offering.description: Which of the agent's jobs to try; the service picks one when it is not given.

answer.description: The agent's answer, or what went wrong, in words.

ms.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

kept.description: It was kept as a test.

sent_back.description: It was said to be wrong, and sent back.

ArtifactId.description: An artifact's id, unique within its build, such as "statement" or "suite". Added in 0.4.

Artifact.description: Something a build has made or will make: one per stage output. Added in 0.4.

name.description: Its name as a person reads it, such as "Statement of the job".

by.description: Who makes it, in words: the holder's name.

state.description: made: it is there. next: the next one the build will make. later: the build will make it after that. not_made: its stage ran, or the build ended, and it was not made (summary.words says why). not_run: its stage is in the lifecycle and the service does not run it (summary.words says why).

kind.description: What it is, which says the shape of its summary. A client that does not know a kind reads summary.words, or the name. as_built was added in 0.4.6.

version.description: Which version of it, in words, such as "v4" or a short commit.

digest.description: Its digest, as sha256:<hex>, when it has one.

summary.description: What it says, readable, never raw file content. The shape is the kind's: spec SpecSummary (added in 0.4.8), statement StatementSummary, suite SuiteSummary, programs ProgramsSummary, findings FindingsSummary, security SecuritySummary, package PackageSummary, run_plan RunPlanSummary, as_built AsBuiltSummary (added in 0.4.6), any other kind or any artifact not made WordsSummary.

files.description: The files it is, at links the service answers with the same key.

StatementSummary.description: The statement of the job, from the agent's own files. Added in 0.4.

open.description: The questions the spec writer left for the person.

features.description: The feature list the statement carries: every feature approved, and every one proposed and not yet approved. Added in 0.4.3.

ProgramsSummary.description: The programs Code wrote. Added in 0.4.

does.description: What the script says it does.

commit.description: The commit they are from, short.

pr.description: The pull request they were written on.

FindingsSummary.description: The code critic's findings. Added in 0.4.

open.description: The findings still open, each to answer by a change or a reason.

outside.description: Notes outside the change, which hold nothing up.

reach.description: What the agent may reach, each with its access and reason.

RunPlanSummary.description: The run plan: for each stage after Package, who holds it. Added in 0.4.

holder.description: The holder's name; null when nobody holds the role.

reads.description: chosen, not chosen, or not used.

WordsSummary.description: Any other artifact, or one not made: what it is or why it is not there, in words. Added in 0.4.

SpecSummary.description: The spec of Requirements (spec-v1), readable: the product, each feature with its requirements and acceptance scenarios in words, the interfaces and which must be kept, the constraints, and the open questions. Added in 0.4.8.

AsBuiltSummary.description: The as-built record of Reverse engineering (stages.json 1.4.0), readable: its source, why it was made, and its five parts, each in words with one short line per item. It says what the code is, never whether it is right. Added in 0.4.6.

source.description: What the record is tied to.

repository.description: The repository, as a URL or owner/name, or the folder it was read from.

commit.description: The commit digest the record describes.

ran.description: Whether the code was also run, not only read.

trigger.description: adoption: the codebase was taken on. drift: the code changed outside the lifecycle, and the record says only what changed since the last one.

since.description: drift: the commit of the record before, which this one is described against.

brought.description: Present when the record was brought to the build with the starting point as-built-record, made elsewhere and not by this build's Reverse engineering. Added in 0.4.7.

from.description: Where it was read: a folder, or a repository, commit and path.

words.description: Such as "Brought from /work/records/word-counter. The code it describes is not taken on; Code writes the code fresh."

parts.description: The five parts, once each, in this order: behaviors, architecture, interfaces, dependencies, tests_and_gaps.

AsBuiltPart.description: One part of the as-built record, readable. Added in 0.4.6.

name.description: Such as "Behaviors" or "Existing tests and gaps".

count.description: How many things the part lists: behaviors, parts of the architecture, interfaces, components, or tests and gaps.

words.description: The part in a sentence or two, such as "4 behaviors, each with its evidence".

items.description: One short line per item, each naming its evidence where the record does, such as "B2 Counts the words: splits on spaces (scripts/count.mjs:4)". A gap reads as one, such as "Gap: ...".

file.description: The path of the part's file among the artifact's files, such as as-built/behaviors.json.

StartSource.description: The codebase a build starts from: a repository, at a commit when one is named, or a local folder for local use. One of repository or folder. For the starting point as-built-record (added in 0.4.7) it names the as-built record instead: a local folder holding the record's files (record.json and its five parts), or a repository, a commit and the path of the record's folder in it. Added in 0.4.6.

repository.description: A git URL, or owner/name on GitHub.

commit.description: The commit to start from. Absent means the repository's newest commit, which the service reads and records.

folder.description: A folder on the service's own computer, for a service that runs locally. A service that does not read local folders refuses the request and says so.

path.description: as-built-record: the folder in the repository that holds the record's files, such as as-built; absent means the repository's top. Added in 0.4.7.

BuildSource.description: The codebase a build knew, at the commit it knew. Added in 0.4.6.

starting_point.description: The starting point the build came from, such as existing-code or as-built-record.

record.description: as-built-record: where the as-built record was read, a folder or a repository, commit and path. repository and commit then name the code the record describes, which the build did not take on. Added in 0.4.7.

trigger.description: Why the build reverse engineered the code: it was taken on, or it changed outside the lifecycle.

commit.description: The commit the build knew: a git commit, or sha256:<hex> of a folder that is not a git repository.

ProductSource.description: The codebase of a product and the last commit any of its builds knew, and whether the code changed since, as far as the service can read it now. A client shows the words beside the when-needed Reverse engineering action. Added in 0.4.6.

commit.description: The last commit any build knew.

current.description: The repository's commit now; null when the service could not read it (words says why).

drift.description: Whether current differs from commit: the code changed outside the lifecycle.

words.description: Such as "The code changed outside the lifecycle: the repository is at 9b1c2d4, and the last build knew 3f2a9c1."

AsBuilt.description: Marks a feature or a proposal as a behavior of the as-built record: what the code does, never a judgment of it. Added in 0.4.6.

behavior.description: The behavior's id in the as-built record.

evidence.description: What the claim stands on, such as a file and line or an observed run.

change.description: On drift: the behavior is new since the last record, changed, or no longer there.

FixItem.description: A proposed fix: a behavior of the as-built record the person said is a bug. It is a backlog item linked to the behavior, and a change to fix it goes through Requirements like any other; nothing approves it silently. Added in 0.4.6.

feature.description: The feature the behavior was proposed as.

behavior.description: The behavior's id in the as-built record.

does.description: What the code does today, as the record says.

words.description: The person's words on what is wrong, when they gave some.

state.description: proposed: waiting to be taken up. A later version may add more.

build.description: The build it was kept on.

BuildState.description: Where a build stands as a whole. Added in 0.4.

name.description: The product's name: the name its builds share. Not a project, which is the lifecycle's team scope.

BuildAt.description: The stage a build is at, as the build list's at. Added in 0.4.

run_plan.description: The run plan of the newest build that has one.

activity.description: One line per stage event, newest first: a short feed, not the chat.

setup.description: Every setup stage of stages.json, once each, in its order: who holds it for the product now, with what settings, and since which version. Added in 0.4.2.

when_needed.description: Every when_needed stage of stages.json, once each, in its order: whether the service can run it on the product now, and why not when it cannot. Added in 0.4.2.

words.description: Such as "0.1.0 runs again: rolled back from 0.2.0".

running.description: The version that runs now, as far as the service knows: the newest one installed that was not rolled back or retired; null when none is. Added in 0.4.4.

retired.description: Present once the product is decommissioned: nothing of it runs, its records are kept, and its when-needed actions cannot run. Added in 0.4.4.

version.description: The version that ran when it was retired.

source.description: The product's codebase and the last commit any build knew, when a build knew one. Added in 0.4.6.

SetupForm.description: The small form a person fills in to set up one stage: who may hold it, a few settings with sensible defaults, and the question a client sends the product's boss for it. It is saved with PUT /roles/{role}: the holder chosen, with this stage's values under the stage's id in the holder's settings, beside any other stage the same role holds (lifecycle document 0.1, Holder.settings). Added in 0.4.4.

ask.description: The question "Ask the boss" sends for this stage, such as "Who should monitor word-counter?".

reference_agent.description: The role's reference agent, when it has one; a client offers it as a holder only then.

shares.description: When the role holds another setup stage too, such as the watcher holding Monitor and Cost: words saying one holder holds both, each with its own settings.

SetupField.description: One setting of a setup form. Added in 0.4.4.

name.description: The setting's name in the holder's settings for the stage.

kind.description: number: saved as a JSON number. text: words. choice: one of options.

default.description: The value filled in until the person changes it, and saved when they leave it.

unit.description: Words after a number, such as minutes or percent.

WhenNeededConfirm.description: The card a person reads before a when-needed action runs: what will happen, in the stage's own words, who may act, and what cannot be undone. A client shows it on the button's press and takes the action only on the person's confirm; when you_may is false it shows who_may and does not offer the confirm. Added in 0.4.4.

will.description: What will happen: the stage's hands_back in stages.json.

steps.description: What the service will do, step by step, for this product now.

who_may.description: Who may take it: the lifecycle's approvers for the stage, read as for a gate, in words.

you_may.description: Whether the person asking may take it.

from_version.description: The version it acts on, the one that runs.

to_version.description: For Rollback, the version it goes back to; for Impact, the changed version it compares.

cannot_undo.description: What cannot be undone, each named, as Rollback's own words ask; empty when nothing is known.

changes.description: For Reconfigure: each stage whose holder or settings in the setup chosen now differ from the run plan the running version has.

WhenNeededLast.description: The last time a when-needed action ran on the product, done or refused. Added in 0.4.4.

version.description: The version of the build it ran on.

files.description: What it handed back, such as the impact report.

SetupItem.description: One stage set up once per product, as the product's lifecycle has it now: the lifecycle of the project its newest build was started under, or the organization's. A holder is chosen with the roles operations, for the organization or that project. Added in 0.4.2.

role.description: The role whose holder holds the stage, one of the stage's role_ids; PUT /roles/{role} chooses it.

project.description: The project whose lifecycle this is, the newest build's; null for the organization's.

state.description: chosen: a holder holds the role. not_chosen: nobody does, so the stage is for the person to set up. not_used: the lifecycle leaves the stage out.

holder.description: Who holds it; null unless chosen.

settings.description: The holder's settings, as names and values; empty when it has none or none is chosen. From 0.4.4, when the holder keeps settings under this stage's id, these are that entry; otherwise its settings that are no stage's entry.

since.description: The version of the product's earliest build, in an unbroken run up to its newest, whose holder and settings for the stage are the ones chosen now; null when no build has used this choice yet (it holds from the next version), and for a stage not chosen or not used.

words.description: What a person reads, such as "Unchanged since 0.1.0" or "Nobody chosen".

form.description: The form a person sets the stage up with. Added in 0.4.4.

WhenNeededItem.description: One action on the product, run when something happens. A client draws its button enabled only when can_run is true, and then takes the build's own action with the actions operation; otherwise it draws it disabled with why_not. Added in 0.4.2.

can_run.description: Whether the service can run it on the product now.

why_not.description: Why it cannot, in words. Present exactly when can_run is false.

action.description: The action that runs it: one the named build offers at this stage now, posted as /builds/{build}/actions/{name}. Present exactly when can_run is true. From 0.4.4 the action may be the product's own when-needed action, named by the stage's id, which the build need not list among its actions; its needs are listed here.

needs.description: What the action is sent with, such as the version to roll back to and why. Added in 0.4.4.

confirm.description: The confirm card. Present only when can_run is true. Added in 0.4.4.

last.description: The last time it ran on the product, when it has. Added in 0.4.4.

StageWorkspace.description: One stage of a build as a workspace. Added in 0.4.

state.description: The same as the build's stage.

given.description: The artifacts of earlier stages it was given, as ids in the build's artifacts, only those made.

outputs.description: The build's artifacts this stage makes.

done_when.description: What done means for the stage: its done_when in stages.json.

cadence.description: The stage's cadence in stages.json, the same as the build's stage. Added in 0.4.2.

carried.description: The same as the build's stage. Added in 0.4.2.

features.description: The stage's features on this build, one short line each, under the same conditions as the build's stage features. Added in 0.4.5.

StageGate.description: The last time the stage waited on a person, or waits now. Absent when it never has. Added in 0.4.

actions.description: Open: the names of the build's actions at this stage that this person may take now, so its buttons are the build's. Answered: the actions it offered.

answered.description: Who answered it, when, and with which action. Absent on an open gate, and on one that closed without an answer (closed says why).

closed.description: Why it closed without an answer, such as a newer push to the pull request.

who_may.description: Who may answer it, in words.

open.description: At Requirements: what the statement still leaves open for the person, such as its price. Added in 0.4.3.

features.description: At Requirements, when the build carries features: what the gate starts building with. Features already approved in a chat are listed as approved and not asked about again; approving the gate approves to_approve; backlog stays proposed. Added in 0.4.3.

MessagesAnswer.description: A stage's chat, oldest first. Added in 0.4.

Message.description: One message in a stage's chat. Added in 0.4.

build.description: The build it was said in.

kind.description: system: the service itself, such as when the agent could not answer.

role.description: The role an agent answers as. "boss" marks a directive the product's boss posted into this chat on the person's behalf (added in 0.4.1).

features.description: The new or changed features the agent proposes in this reply, each with its own answer. Added in 0.4.3.

Proposal.description: A change the agent proposes: one of the build's existing actions, with its needs filled. The person takes it with the actions operation. Added in 0.4.

action.description: The action's name, one the build offers this person now.

needs.description: The action's request, one member per need.

MessageRequest.description: What the person says to the agent holding a stage. Added in 0.4.

build.description: The build it is about; the product's newest when absent.

MessageReplyAnswer.description: The person's message as kept, and the reply. Added in 0.4.

BossMessagesAnswer.description: The conversation with the product's boss, oldest first. Added in 0.4.1.

BossMessage.description: One message between a person and the product's boss. Added in 0.4.1.

build.description: The product's newest build when it was said.

kind.description: agent: the boss. system: the service itself, such as when the boss could not answer.

confirms.description: On a person's message: the proposal it confirmed.

declines.description: On a person's message: the proposal it declined.

plan.description: The stages a larger request touches, in the order the lifecycle runs them.

started.description: The build the boss started, only on the person's confirmation of a start_version proposal.

dropped.description: Each stage the boss told that withdrawn work is no longer wanted, with the message it posted there.

features.description: The new or changed features the boss proposes in this reply, each with its own answer. Added in 0.4.3.

BossRoute.description: Where the boss posted: the stage's chat, the message it posted there, and the build it was posted on. Added in 0.4.1.

BossPlanStep.description: One stage of a plan: what it must do, and the gate the person meets there when it has one. Added in 0.4.1.

gate.description: The gate the person meets at this stage, and who may answer it. Absent when the stage has none.

BossProposal.description: What the boss proposes. action is one of the build's existing actions, which the person takes with the actions operation, or start_version, which asks to start the product's next version with that build as its prototype and is confirmed with confirms on this operation. Added in 0.4.1.

build.description: The build the action applies to; for start_version, the build the next version starts from.

needs.description: The action's request, one member per need; for start_version, version.

words.description: The proposal as a question to the person, such as "Start version 0.2.0?".

when.description: When the build will offer the action, if it does not offer it yet, such as the changes action on a version that has just started. A client shows the proposal and lets the person confirm it once the build offers the action.

state.description: On a kept message: open until the person answers it; closed when it can no longer be taken, such as when a newer proposal replaced it.

BossMessageRequest.description: What the person says to the boss, and the proposal it confirms or declines, if any. Added in 0.4.1.

confirms.description: The id of an open start_version proposal the person says yes to.

declines.description: The id of an open proposal the person says no to.

BossReplyAnswer.description: The person's message as kept, and the boss's reply. Added in 0.4.1.

BossCommitmentsAnswer.description: Everything the boss committed on the person's behalf, oldest first, never a selection. Added in 0.4.1.

BossCommitment.description: One thing the boss committed: what, to whom, and when. Added in 0.4.1.

kind.description: routed: a directive posted into a stage's chat. proposed: a proposal made to the person. started: a build started on the person's confirmation. dropped: a stage told that work is no longer wanted.

to.description: Whom, in words: the agent at a stage, or the person.

reply.description: The boss's message it was made in.

message_id.description: routed and dropped: the message posted in the stage's chat.

withdraws.description: dropped: the commitment whose work was withdrawn.

confirmation.description: started: the person's message that confirmed it.

FeatureId.description: A feature's id: stable across the product's versions and never given to another feature, such as F3. Added in 0.4.3.

Feature.description: One feature of the statement of the job. Added in 0.4.3.

does.description: What it does, in one sentence.

offering.description: The offering of the statement it belongs to, by name.

FeatureProposal.description: A new or changed feature proposed in a reply, and where its answer stands, as the person reading it sees it. Added in 0.4.3.

proposal.description: The proposal's id, which the feature operations name.

feature.description: The feature's id: a new feature's is given when it is proposed.

was.description: changed: the feature as it was approved before.

state.description: open: not answered yet. asked: someone asked the approvers, and it waits on them. approved: approved, in a chat or by the Requirements gate. not_now: left for later, a backlog item. replaced: a newer proposal of the same feature came after it. bug: a behavior marked as built that the person said is a bug, kept as a fix item (added in 0.4.6). dropped: a behavior marked as built that the person dropped (added in 0.4.6).

you_may_approve.description: Whether the person reading it may answer the Requirements gate, so may approve it. One who may not asks instead.

approvers.description: Who may approve it, in words; empty when anyone may.

decision.description: bug and dropped were added in 0.4.6.

tests.description: When the features were listed after the build: the tests already in its suite that the proposer says check this feature, each one of the suite's names exactly. A test whose name or content does not make that clear is left out, never guessed. Added in 0.4.5.

as_built.description: Present when the proposal is a behavior of the as-built record. A client offers Approve feature (the behavior is intended), This is a bug and Drop on it. Added in 0.4.6.

fix.description: bug: the fix item kept for it. Added in 0.4.6.

FeatureBackfillRequest.description: Asks for a product's features to be listed from its statement of the job. Nothing is needed. Added in 0.4.5.

FeatureApproveAllRequest.description: Approves several feature proposals at once. Added in 0.4.5.

proposals.description: The proposals approved, each once, at most one per feature.

message.description: The message they were approved on, when it was in a chat.

FeatureApproveAllAnswer.description: The proposals approved, as the person now sees them, and each feature after the answer. Added in 0.4.5.

statement.description: The statement of the job's new version, with every feature approved: one version for the whole answer.

FeatureCount.description: How many of the product's features a stage covers on a build. Added in 0.4.5.

covered.description: Requirements: features approved. Test: approved features with a test. Code: approved features whose tests all pass. Review: approved features with no open finding tied to them. Docs: approved features the docs name.

total.description: Requirements: features proposed or approved, leaving out those only in the backlog. Every other stage: approved features.

words.description: The count in words, short, such as "4 of 5 features".

FeatureSliceItem.description: One feature at one stage. Added in 0.4.5.

state.description: done: the stage covers it. to_do: it does not yet, such as a feature with no test. failing: tests checking it fail. stale: covered as it was before it changed. findings: Review has open findings tied to it.

words.description: Short, such as "6 of 6 passing" or "No test yet: to do".

tests.description: Test: the tests that check it.

passed.description: Code: how many of its tests passed in the newest round that ran them.

of.description: Code: how many tests check it.

findings.description: Review: the findings tied to it through its tests: the place names a line inside one of its tests, or the finding quotes a test's name.

open.description: False for a note outside the change, which holds nothing up.

FeatureSlice.description: A stage's features on a build. Added in 0.4.5.

words.description: The same as the build's stage features.

items.description: Requirements: every feature. Every other stage: each approved feature.

untied.description: Test: the tests that check no feature. Review: the findings tied to no feature. Shown as not tied to a feature; never guessed.

FeatureDecisionRequest.description: An answer to one feature proposal. Added in 0.4.3.

message.description: The message the answer was given on, when it was answered in a chat.

words.description: bug: what is wrong with the behavior, in the person's words, kept on the fix item. Added in 0.4.6.

FeatureDecisionAnswer.description: The feature after the answer, and the proposal as the person now sees it. Added in 0.4.3.

statement.description: approve: the statement of the job's new version, with the feature in it.

fix.description: bug: the fix item kept. Added in 0.4.6.

FeatureEntry.description: A feature as the product holds it now. Added in 0.4.3.

state.description: approved: approved at least once; a change waiting for an answer is pending. proposed: never approved yet.

backlog.description: True when its newest proposal was left for later (not now).

pending.description: The proposal waiting for an answer, when one is.

as_built.description: Present when the feature came from the as-built record. Added in 0.4.6.

fix.description: Present when its behavior as built was said to be a bug. Added in 0.4.6.

dropped.description: Present when its behavior as built was dropped. Added in 0.4.6.

FeatureCell.description: One feature against one artifact. Added in 0.4.3.

state.description: done: the artifact covers the feature as approved. stale: it covers an older version of the feature, or was made before an artifact it depends on changed. missing: it does not cover the feature, or is not made. failing: tests naming the feature fail.

tests.description: tests and code: the tests naming the feature, and how many passed in the newest round that ran them (passed is null when none has).

link.description: Where the artifact is opened at this feature.

FeatureRow.description: One feature of the matrix. Added in 0.4.3.

badge.description: Against the product's version before this one: new when it was not approved there, changed when its name, what it does or its offering differ, unchanged otherwise.

pending.description: The proposal waiting for an answer, as the person reading it sees it, so a client can answer it beside the list. Added in 0.4.5.

from.description: Where its newest proposal was said: the message, in the chat of the stage named, or the boss's when none is. Added in 0.4.5.

tests.description: The tests in this build's suite that check it: those whose names start with its id, and those mapped to it when the features were listed after the build. Present when the build has a suite. Added in 0.4.5.

as_built.description: Present when the feature came from the as-built record. Added in 0.4.6.

fix.description: Present when its behavior as built was said to be a bug. Added in 0.4.6.

dropped.description: Present when its behavior as built was dropped. Added in 0.4.6.

FeaturesAnswer.description: The features matrix for one build of a product. Added in 0.4.3.

build.description: The build the matrix is for.

versions.description: The product's versions, newest first, each once, for a version filter.

columns.description: The columns, in this order: spec, tests, code, review, docs.

words.description: When there are no features, how they are added.

unmapped.description: The tests in this build's suite that check no feature: neither named nor mapped. Present when the build has a suite and features. Added in 0.4.5.

backfill.description: Whether the product's features can be listed from its statement of the job now (POST /builds/{id}/features/backfill), and in words what that does or why not. Offered only for a product with no features yet. Added in 0.4.5.

fixes.description: The fix items kept for the product up to this build: behaviors as built the person said are bugs. Present when there is at least one. Added in 0.4.6.

FeatureHistoryEntry.description: One thing that happened to a feature. Added in 0.4.3.

kind.description: proposed, approved, not_now, asked, bug, dropped: its proposals and their answers (bug and dropped added in 0.4.6). spec, tests, code, review, docs: an artifact that covers it was made or changed.

link.description: message: the chat message, at its stage (no stage for the boss's conversation). artifact: the artifact, opened at this feature.

FeatureAnswer.description: One feature and its history, oldest first. Added in 0.4.3.
